body:
generateMutants reports a plainly mutable line as unmutable, and hollow-test's diff-scoped gate then refuses the whole run as unverifiable (#658's fail-closed firing on a false premise). Measured on this repo: 27.8% of non-comment code lines were mutable; 4,176 lines — 9.5 percentage points — had NO mutant of any kind.

ROOT CAUSE: the eight operators in packages/core/lib/mutate.mjs are invert-comparison, bool-flip, null-return, off-by-one, logic-swap, negate-guard-subclause, array-literal-shrink and ternary-swap. A line like `const tag = randomUUID();` has no comparison, boolean, return, numeric literal, array literal or ternary, so nothing matches. SKIP_LINE (mutate.mjs:401) additionally skips import lines by design.

WHAT TO BUILD

Add a `value-substitute` operator: for `const NAME = <rhs>;`, replace the rhs with `undefined`. If no test notices the bound value vanishing, the coverage over that line is hollow — which is exactly what the gate exists to detect.

TWO DESIGN CONSTRAINTS, both measured, both load-bearing:

1. FALLBACK, not a ninth entry in OPERATORS. generateMutants pushes one mutant per matching operator, so adding it to OPERATORS would give a second, redundant mutant to every line the existing set already covers. Run it only for a line that every operator above declined, so the new mutants are exactly the lines that previously had none. Export FALLBACK_OPERATORS alongside OPERATORS — core.test.mjs already imports OPERATORS and the two should be testable the same way.

2. `const` ONLY — not let/var. A let/var initializer is routinely overwritten on every path before it is read (`let out = ''; ... out = run();`), so substituting its value is an EQUIVALENT mutant: it survives while changing nothing, which is a FALSE gate failure. Measured: including let/var produced 16 survivors in a 141-mutant sample, 2 of them exactly that shape; restricting to const gave 137 mutants and 14 survivors, all real. A const binding is single-assignment, so its value is the one the rest of the scope actually sees.

WRITE THE RED TESTS FIRST in packages/core/test/core.test.mjs, beside the existing generateMutants tests:
  - `const tag = randomUUID();` yields exactly one mutant, operator `value-substitute`, mutating to `const tag = undefined;`
  - a line the existing operators DO cover (e.g. `if (a > b) {`) gains NO value-substitute mutant — proving the fallback does not double-cover
  - `let out = '';` and `var x = f();` yield no value-substitute mutant — proving the equivalent-mutant class is excluded
  - `const x = undefined;` and `const x = null;` yield none — already the sentinel, substitution says nothing
  - an import line still yields none (SKIP_LINE unchanged)
Each must fail against the current mutate.mjs. Demonstrate that by reverting the operator and showing the tests go red.

DO NOT change packages/hollow-test/** or scripts/mutation-gate.mjs. Both are declared rails: this change must be transparent to the consumer, and if either needs editing to accommodate it, the operator is wrong. Their existing tests (diff-zero-mutants.test.mjs, starved-budget.test.mjs) assert the zero-mutant refusal and must keep passing — the refusal is correct behaviour and is NOT being relaxed.

MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, for the reviewer: mutants repo-wide 17,717 -> 21,893 (+23.6%); line mutability 27.8% -> 37.3%. Survival on a 137-mutant sample across spec-lint, coldstart, premortem and consensus-fix was 14 (10%), and all 14 were triaged as REAL hollow coverage — seven of the shape 'value computed then handed to a sink no test asserts', seven of the shape 'CLI flag parsed but never exercised through the binary'. Because the gate is diff-scoped, these do not fail existing code; they apply when someone next edits such a line.

ACCEPTANCE
- The five red tests above pass, and fail when the operator is reverted.
- `const tag = randomUUID();` produces a mutant where it previously produced none.
- A line already covered by an existing operator gains no second mutant.
- packages/hollow-test's own tests still pass unchanged, proving the zero-mutant refusal is intact.
- `npm test` green from the repo root, output shown.
- `adlc rails-guard --base origin/main --ticket <this ticket id>` exits 0, proving hollow-test and mutation-gate.mjs were not touched.
title: mutate: add a value-substitute fallback operator so const assignments are mutable (#1013)
